sentences.span: We remind investors that oil prices are somewhat elevated but refined product prices (and crack spreads) are near record levels
sentences.why: GS's drone-attack note documents exactly this divergence: crude headline-risk elevated while refined product/crack spreads are separately at records, i.e. the two have come apart.

sentences.span: Markets seem to react positively to any story, rumor, or hope that is positive.
sentences.why: Tchir's note (in the same Houthi/Hormuz oil-disruption context the pulse is covering) states markets reprice instantly and favorably on any positive rumor, matching the sentence's claim about a ceasefire rumor repricing barrels the market fears losing.

sentences.span: China absorbed ~25% of the 20mb/d that transited the Strait; remove that shock absorber and GIR says fair value is roughly $10-15 higher
sentences.why: The 'fair value' framing traces to Jared Cohen citing GS's own research arm (GIR), not JPMorgan. There is no JPMorgan document anywhere in this day's source corpus (checked every .meta.json source field) — the bank attribution is fabricated.

sentences.span: last week’s FOMC meeting, where policymakers delivered a widely expected rate increase but signalled a more hawkish policy outlook
sentences.why: Fed hiked Sept 17 ("last week" from the Sept 21 pulse date); BoJ also hiked Sept 18 per the Allianz calendar row (17190). Both central banks hiked in the prior week, supporting the plural "central banks that hiked last week."

sentences.span: On the Trump-Xi meeting, the only thing that matters is any signal Xi is shifting away from ‘playing for time’
sentences.why: The Trump-Xi/oil-premium link is a real GS (Jared Cohen) view, but attributed here to JPMorgan (no JPM source exists in the corpus) and the figure is changed from GS's "$10-15" to "$16." The BofA short-2yr-Treasury ($SHY) claim has zero support anywhere in the corpus (no "SHY", "fund manager survey"/FMS, or "not restrictive enough" language tied to BofA).

This describes the pulse's own prior trade-board call ("this pulse carried from last Monday") — internal editorial history, not a claim any source PDF makes. No document contains a long-oil call closed at a loss.

sentences.span: increasing their 2027 estimates for global Hyperscaler issuance $400bn to $420bn, a reflection of some modest increased in CapEx forecasts
sentences.why: GS credit note shows hyperscaler bond issuance funding AI capex is rising sharply, and 17193 separately documents FCF pressure from GenAI capex — together supporting the bondholders-fund-the-marginal-dollar claim.

sentences.span: Jared Cohen (President of Global Affairs & Co-Head, GS Global Institute) on US-China
sentences.why: No specific figure/attribution/direction to break; the corpus itself shows genuine internal diversity of view within the same house (e.g. GS Crook's multi-desk quotes vs GS Coppersmith's cautious equities note), supporting the generic claim that a counter-view originates inside the same banks.

No document mentions a BofA fund manager survey ("FMS" does not appear anywhere in the corpus) or a 33% overinvestment reading. No document states Goldman semiconductor gross margins at 70% vs a 55% 15-year average — "70%" near "margin", "55%", and "15-year average" all return nothing relevant.

sentences.span: Markets are now pricing in a greater than 50% chance of a hike in October and three more hikes this cycle
sentences.why: MS states October hike odds are just above 50%, which "coin flip" faithfully paraphrases (near-even odds).

sentences.span: it's hard to not look at two-year yields approaching 4.75% and say they are attractive
sentences.why: "Approaching 4.75%" matches "4.744%" under the value-not-characters matching rule; the conditional logic (no October hike kills the second-hike call, yields come down) is a reasonable inference built on the same document's ">50% chance" and "three more hikes" framing.

sentences.span: In the US, funds sold Semis, broader AI Tech, Discretionary and Industrials / Energy exposures, while adding to Hyperscalers, Optical Networking, Cybersecurity, Financials and Materials
sentences.why: The rotation direction (out of semis, into financials) is directly supported by MS PB flow data for the past week, but that data describes one week's flow, not a trend running "since the Nasdaq peaked in early June." No document mentions a Nasdaq peak in early June.

sentences.span: Less than 30% of S&P stocks are now above the 50-day moving average
sentences.why: GS Coppersmith directly documents deteriorating breadth alongside a resilient headline index and net equity buying (not selling) — exactly the "damage spread across the average stock while a few names carry the index" / "not panic selling" framing.

sentences.span: The BoJ delivered a 25bp rate hike, citing rising upside inflation risks. Sato and Asada dissented in favour of no policy change
sentences.why: The 1.25% rate and two dissents (Sato, Asada) are confirmed (consistent with a 7-2 vote on a 9-member board). But "highest since 1995" and "both dissents coming from board members appointed by Prime Minister Takaichi" appear nowhere in the corpus — no document mentions 1995 in connection with BoJ rates, and no document ties Sato/Asada to Takaichi appointments.

sentences.span: The US August inflation reports came in above expectations, with core inflation accelerating by 0.3% month-on-month versus the 0.2% consensus forecast
sentences.why: No document contains the figures 1.7%/1.8% for August core inflation, and no document names UBS and Goldman both calling the next hike for January 2027. The one source that does describe the August core inflation surprise says it came in ABOVE expectations (a beat), the opposite direction implied by the pulse's "does not force the next move" framing.
